candidate: Low-dose L-tryptophan + nicotinic acid + nicotinamide mixture (Connell et al. 2021)
disposition: Retain as bounded counterevidence to generic NAD-precursor claims; not a niacin monotherapy test, BUB1B candidate, or Track 2 nominee.
route: NAD-precursor mixture; no BUBR1-restoration mechanism tested.
identity_boundary: The intervention combined L-tryptophan, nicotinic acid and nicotinamide. Results cannot be attributed to nicotinic acid alone or transferred to NMN, NR, other niacin doses, or retail products.

primary_study.citation: Connell NJ et al. NAD+-Precursor Supplementation With L-Tryptophan, Nicotinic Acid, and Nicotinamide Does Not Affect Mitochondrial Function or Skeletal Muscle Function in Physically Compromised Older Adults. J Nutr. 2021;151(10):2917-2931.
primary_study.design: Randomized, double-blind, controlled crossover; each period 32 days with at least five weeks washout.
primary_study.population: Community-dwelling physically compromised adults aged at least 65; 14 actual participants in the registry, 13 described in the paper, outcome-specific n=11-13. Not selected for NAD deficiency or a neuromuscular diagnosis.
primary_study.intervention: Reported 207.5 mg/day niacin equivalents: L-tryptophan 210 mg/day, nicotinic acid 4 mg/day, and nicotinamide 200 mg/day.
primary_study.comparator: Amino-acid mixture resembling the whey-protein source without the three tested NAD precursors.

outcomes.muscle_methyl_nicotinamide: Increased under intervention, P=.001; marker compatible with altered NAD turnover, not proof of increased NAD availability or BUBR1 engagement.
outcomes.mitochondrial_respiration: No benefit in ADP-stimulated respiration, P=.716, or maximal uncoupled respiration, P=.495. Abstract and main text give discrepant net exercise-efficiency P values (.342 and .636 respectively); discrepancy retained unresolved.
outcomes.physical_function: SPPB balance, gait, chair-rise and total-score comparisons nonpositive. One perceived-physical-function RAND-36 domain favored intervention, P=.031, n=12; other reported domains nonpositive. Figure caption says eight domains while Discussion says one of nine; multiplicity adjustment not identified.
outcomes.body_composition_and_volume: No reported intervention-control difference in body composition or vastus lateralis volume.
outcomes.exercise_and_energy: No reported benefit in exercise energy expenditure, substrate use or efficiency.
outcomes.tolerability: 100% intervention sachets and 99% control sachets reported consumed; one cold sore resolved without intervention. Short, small study does not establish broader safety.

limitations: The intervention is a mixture, so the effect of nicotinic acid cannot be isolated.
Nicotinic acid was only 4 mg/day, far below the 750-1000 mg/day niacin dose in Pirinen et al.; this is not a high-dose niacin monotherapy failure test.
No BUB1B/BUBR1, checkpoint, chromosome-fidelity, or MVA endpoint was measured.
Functional outcomes were secondary/exploratory; the sample-size calculation concerned primary mitochondrial respiration, not those functional endpoints.
The sole perceived-function positive was one among multiple RAND-36 domains; no multiplicity correction was identified.
The sample was small, follow-up was 32 days per condition, and some assays used only 11-13 participants.
Abstract/main-text P values disagree for net exercise efficiency; RAND-36 domain count also differs between caption and discussion.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists the study as terminated after COVID-19 disruption and posts no results.
primary_study.source_scope: Complete Europe PMC XML scientific text, figure captions, methods, results and discussion; PubMed record; current ClinicalTrials.gov API record. Figure images and historical registry versions were not inspected.

competitive_interpretation.versus_niacin: No direct BUB1B/BUBR1 evidence and no objective function benefit, but it does not test high-dose nicotinic acid monotherapy. It supports compound- and dose-specific evaluation rather than class-wide precursor equivalence.
competitive_interpretation.versus_apitegromab: No objective muscle-function positive; apitegromab has stronger pediatric motor-function evidence in SMA, although no MVA transfer is established.
competitive_interpretation.nomination_decision: Do not add as a Track 2 nominee or alter the provisional niacin/apitegromab pair. Retain as a niacin counterevidence qualification.

source_files.scope: Current registry design, status, intervention, outcomes, enrollment and posting history fields.

next_evidence_gates: Keep nicotinic acid, nicotinamide, NMN, NR and mixtures as distinct interventions in the next comparative BUBR1 study.
Measure muscle NAD pathway engagement, allele-specific BUBR1 abundance/function, absolute muscle output, renewal and chromosome fidelity at justified exposure.
Do not use this mixture trial as a negative test of high-dose niacin or as evidence for MVA efficacy.
